newsitem.title: SURINAM: Suriname sees mining boosting export income 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Suriname sees mining boosting export income 40 pct.

text.p: New developments in oil and mining activities could boost Suriname's export revenues by 40 percent to $700 million per year over the next few years, a leading government official said Thursday.
Natural Resources Minister Errol Alibux highlighted developments in gold and granite mining as paving the way to better export revenues for the country.
Addressing a four day mining conference Alibux said that granite mining has the potential to bring in $25 per year.
Gold mining, which just a few years ago was negligible, was already producing 15 tonnes per year and revenues of $180 million per year, he said.
Oil production has also grown rapidly to 9,500 barrels per day and annual revenues of $44 million, he added.
The growth in new activities offsets the decline of Suriname's key bauxite and alumina industry.
Suriname has slipped from the world's top bauxite producer with 15 percent of world production in the 1940s to just two percent now, Alibux said.

Even in the 1980s bauxite revenues accounted for 80 percent of the state's total income. Top production levels of 7.2 million tonnes of bauxite per year in 1974 have plummeted to 1.7 million tonnes, bringing in revenues of $312 million.
